wheel.atl0: the u2 harness's wheel experiment (map-atlas.md §3.2; .cache/map-atlas/critic/wheel.mjs) re-run as .cache/map-atlas/atl0/wheel-atl0.mjs against the production build (pnpm build, then vite preview on localhost) after ATL.0 set wheelPxPerZoomLevel 60 and zoomDelta 1 in src/map/leaflet/LeafletMapAdapter.ts. Headless Chrome over CDP, 1366x768 at DPR 1.5, CPU 1x, the Kalimdor surface. Real CDP mouseWheel events of deltaY -100 every 100 ms at the centre of Durotar's frame, starting from the least zoom (-6) and stopping when the zoom reaches -2. atl0.why: Leaflet 1.9.4 ignores wheel input during its 250 ms zoom animation: two CDP events in three change nothing (the zoom list repeats each value three times), so the trip is capped by the rate per accepted event, 0.5 level at 60 px per level against 0.25 at 120. The smooth wheel of step ATL.8 removes the cap.

rNotch.basis: MEASURED: 2.43 levels from the world fit to the Durotar zone fit at 1366 × 768; at 200 px per level a 100 px notch takes 5 notches (0.59–0.69 s of input at 100 ms) and a 66.67 px notch 8 (0.98–1.13 s). The gate (≤ 8) holds for any notch of 61 px or more (2.43 × 200 / 8). ESTIMATE for the design’s 918 × 700 panel (2.2 levels): 55 px or more. If the owner’s notch proves smaller (a Linux-style 53.3 px notch would take 10), R_notch 160 keeps it at 8. The owner’s notch deltaY remains UNKNOWN, so the value is kept.

rStream.basis: MEASURED: a stream of 30 events (10 px and 30 px, 16 ms apart) was classed as a stream and moved 1.50 and 4.50 levels (200 px per level), every event moving the target. No trackpad trace exists to calibrate against, so the value is kept.

atl9mm8.indexObservation: The minimap index keeps 31 level-0 keys as stored tiles although each is flat navy (0 % of pixels farther than 30 from #0d1b30), while their ancestors at levels −1 to −4 are sea keys (4 at −4, 19 at −3, 30 at −2, 12 at −1). At those levels the key shows the container instead of the tile: no visible change, since both are the same navy. Keys (x, y) at level 0: (1, 22), (3, 60), (3, 79), (5, 51), (5, 52), (7, 1), (7, 2), (26, 1), (26, 2), (40, 88), (47, 74), (47, 87), (49, 8), (49, 68), (55, 47), (71, 28), (71, 47), (71, 74), (73, 62), (75, 55), (96, 87), (98, 85), (106, 82), (108, 76), (110, 74), (112, 10), (112, 37), (114, 16), (114, 28), (114, 53), (114, 70). rNotch.basis: MEASURED: 2.43 levels from the world fit to the Durotar zone fit at 1366 × 768; at 200 px per level a 100 px notch takes 5 notches (0.59–0.69 s of input at 100 ms) and a 66.67 px notch 8 (0.98–1.13 s). The gate (≤ 8) holds for any notch of 61 px or more (2.43 × 200 / 8). ESTIMATE for the design’s 918 × 700 panel (2.2 levels): 55 px or more. If the owner’s notch proves smaller (a Linux-style 53.3 px notch would take 10), R_notch 160 keeps it at 8. The owner’s notch deltaY remains UNKNOWN, so the value is kept.

rStream.basis: MEASURED: a stream of 30 events (10 px and 30 px, 16 ms apart) was classed as a stream and moved 1.50 and 4.50 levels (200 px per level), every event moving the target. No trackpad trace exists to calibrate against, so the value is kept.
